checks.finding: REQ-004 defines `scope` for a cross-cutting override as the approved rule's name (requirements.md:135-156), while AC-030/031 specify only an “approved release-automation” or “release rule” and never give its exact rule name or matching path (acceptance-tests.md:36-37). OQ-002 lists `.github/**` and release/root metadata as shared rules but does not identify a release-automation rule (requirements.md:440-468). Implementers cannot determine the exact valid `scope` value or which paths it covers; this is a Phase 1 product-contract gap, not a design detail.

Investigation.md says OQ-001, OQ-002, OQ-003, OQ-004 and OQ-006 remain carried-forward open questions (investigation.md:87-93), while requirements.md marks these OQs resolved (requirements.md:382-431, 470-516). The disagreement leaves reviewers and implementers unable to determine which component, ownership, promotion, rollback and Pack decisions govern. This conflicts across Phase 1 source artifacts, so it must be resolved in the specification package.

AC-017 combines rejection before 24 hours and acceptance at/after the effective time under one TEST-017 (acceptance-tests.md:23), and AC-018 lists four separately meaningful invalid-sidecar branches under one TEST-018 without individual TEST-ID assertions (acceptance-tests.md:24, 42-44). AC-018a/b cover the registry-change cases but not those four branches separately. Per the Phase 1 authoring sweep, each enumerated branch needs its own concrete test assertion or an explicit reason it is covered elsewhere; otherwise distinct rollback failures can be missed.

The investigation's Open Questions Carried Forward section still presents OQ-001/002/003/004/006 as unresolved (investigation.md:87-93), despite their resolved decisions in requirements.md (requirements.md:382-516). The newer investigation reconciliation does not state that the older list is superseded (investigation.md:95-119). This leaves a stale, uncited-as-historical decision-state claim in a sibling Phase 1 artifact; authors must reconcile it before design/task decomposition.

Spec-Review-Status is Pending (requirements.md:3), but the package cites prior review outputs and Draft tasks: it says edits do not change a review verdict or authorize Draft-task implementation (requirements.md:312-318), says historical review outputs remain unchanged and must be rebound (requirements.md:417-429), and calls sealed round-1 findings historical review evidence (acceptance-tests.md:87-90). Investigation.md has no `## Amendment Re-Review Context` section. The Phase 1 calibration requires that conforming, fully evidenced section to suppress a phase-sequencing finding; without it, the disclosed later-phase evidence crosses the review approval boundary.

Design review would have to invent the exact release-automation rule identity and path scope required by REQ-004/AC-030 (requirements.md:135-157; acceptance-tests.md:36-37). It also cannot safely settle the rollback's zero-registered-identity case: REQ-009 says the solo branch applies “otherwise” (requirements.md:203-206), while resolved OQ-004 defines that branch only for registry count == 1 (requirements.md:497-501), and the tests cover one or multiple identities but not zero (acceptance-tests.md:22-24). These are unresolved product behaviors, not design choices.
